body:
vim-patch:9.2.1114: Visual selection is not highlighted at the cursor position

- In a terminal the character under the cursor was not shown as part of
  the Visual selection. win_line() suppressed the highlight of the
  character under the cursor ("noinvcur"); drop the handling so it is
  highlighted like the rest of the selection.

closes: vim/vim#21317

https://github.com/vim/vim/commit/d10aab4ba6602f8f2f2576d2d62ceb63869db6fb

Nvim gated the suppression on 'guicursor' instead of the GUI
(cursor_is_block_during_visual(), introduced in #8983): the highlight
was suppressed only when the cursor is a non-blinking block. Remove
that helper too, so Visual highlighting no longer depends on
'guicursor'.

Instead of Vim's testdir dumps, update the expected grids of the Nvim
screen tests. Vim's new test
Test_charwise_visual_hl_inclusive_and_exclusive_selection() is not
ported: the updated "Visual highlight" test in
test/functional/ui/highlight_spec.lua already covers the inclusive and
exclusive cases, including the position after `o`. Also remove the
"|Visual| selection highlights the character at cursor." entry from
vim_diff.txt: with this patch Vim highlights it too, so it is no
longer a difference.

Co-authored-by: Shane Harper <shane@shaneharper.net>
AI-assisted

> > Vim's new test Test_charwise_visual_hl_inclusive_and_exclusive_selection() is not ported

Thanks for pointing this out. I didn't properly verify the claim in the PR description that the screen tests already covered this before relying on it. Sorry about that. I've now ported the original test as well (c3c1df6c40).
I mean you should port the test in test_visual.vim verbatim (i.e. to the same file in the same place) instead of rewriting it in Lua.

> I mean you should port the test in test_visual.vim verbatim instead of rewriting it in Lua.

Thanks for the clarification. I'll port the original test verbatim to test/old/testdir/test_visual.vim.
